simple.meaning: פָּזַז (pâzaz) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to solidify (as if by refining); also to spring (as if separating the limbs).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Genesis, 2 Samuel, beginning at Genesis 49:24. The surrounding contexts include family line, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּזַז (H6339) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּזַז (pâzaz) / H6339 is traced through Genesis 49:24, 2 Samuel 6:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6339. pazaz II. [ מָּזַז ] verb be supple, agile (Talmud (rare) מְּזִיזָא hasty ; Arabic be frightened, excited ; Syriac (Lexicons) leap , agile , etc.); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine plural וַיָּ֫פֹזוּ Gen 49:24 , of arms. Pi`el shew agility, leap (in dance), Participle וּמְכַרְכֵּר מְפַזֵּז 2Sam 6:16 .
